statement: For every slice nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever xor_beauty(nums) returns a result r, r is the bitwise XOR of all elements of nums: for every bit position b with 0 <= b < 63, the b-th bit of r is 1 if and only if the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and with the b-th bit of nums[i] equal to 1 is odd. Equivalently, r = nums[0] XOR nums[1] XOR ... XOR nums[len(nums)-1], where XOR denotes bitwise exclusive or.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every slice nums satisfying the preconditions, xor_beauty(nums) returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, go out of bounds, or overflow.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every slice nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever xor_beauty(nums) returns a result r, 0 <= r < 2^30 = 1073741824.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every slice nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever xor_beauty(nums) returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every bit position b with 0 <= b < 63, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) whose b-th bit of nums[i] is 1 is even.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever xor_beauty(nums) returns r and xor_beauty(nums2) returns r2, we have r = r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices of 64-bit integers, each with 1 <= length <= 100000 and all elements between 1 and 1000000000, and nums2 is a permutation of nums (same length and same multiset of values).

statement: Whenever xor_beauty(xs) returns rx, xor_beauty(ys) returns ry, and xor_beauty(nums) returns r, we have r = rx XOR ry, where XOR is bitwise exclusive or (for each bit position the result bit is 1 if and only if exactly one of the two operand bits is 1).
preconditions: xs and ys are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers, each with length between 1 and 100000 and all elements between 1 and 1000000000, and len(xs)+len(ys) <= 100000. Let nums be the concatenation xs ++ ys.

statement: For every slice nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever xor_beauty(nums) returns a result r, r is the bitwise XOR of exactly those distinct values v that occur an odd number of times among the entries of nums. More precisely, for every bit position b with 0 <= b < 63, the b-th bit of r is 1 if and only if the number of distinct values v with 1 <= v <= 1000000000 such that v occurs an odd number of times in nums and the b-th bit of v is 1 is odd. If no value occurs an odd number of times, then r = 0.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
